title: Ember docket: overnight alert follow-ups and playbook TODOs
content:
Quick personal docket from the overnight rotation (notes to self + actionable items). Purpose: collect follow-ups, triage decisions, and short playbook edits before handing off to daytime SREs.

SUMMARY:
- Alerts fired 02:13 UTC: spike in 5xxs from hosted/generation route in eu-central-1. Rate ~6% for ~8 minutes, then auto-mitigated by fallback routing.
- Impact: small subset of customer requests surfaced higher error rates; no full cluster degradation. Some dedicated pools reported elevated GPU OOM logs around same time.
- Triage: promoted hypothesis of a recent model shard change + aggressive batching combo causing transient memory pressure.

TIMELINE (times UTC):
- 02:12:10 alert (metric): generation-5xx-rate > 5%
- 02:13:02 first page to on-call, automated fallback engaged to model-variant-b
- 02:14:30 investigated host metrics (see quick commands below); noticed GPU memory climb on nodes: eu-gpu-pool-3a
- 02:18:40 temporarily drained 2 pods from pool to force rebalancing; 02:22 error rate falling
- 02:25:00 paging quieted; 02:30 closed incident watch, left follow-ups

WHAT I RAN (commands / quick checks):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=pool=eu-gpu-pool-3a
- ssh jump@eu-gpu-03 sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
- curl -s "https://observability/api/metrics?query=rate(generation_5xx[1m])" | jq .
- docker logs --tail 200 model-serving-xyz | grep -i oom

OBSERVATIONS / HYPOTHESIS:
- Two nodes showed sustained memory climbs correlated with a model variant rollout at 01:58 UTC (deploy record: infra/commit/9a3b7).
- Autoscaler did not rebalance fast enough because the new pods requested slightly more vram; scheduler packed pods onto older nodes causing >90% memory on those GPUs.
- Fallback routing and draining pods reduced immediate client impact.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS TAKEN (for safety):
- Drained eu-gpu-pool-3a: triggered re-scheduling (owner: me).
- Pin fallback policy for generation route to use model-variant-stable for next 6 hours (temp mitigation).
- Opened INC-8421 with initial notes and attached 02:12-02:30 slices of metrics.

FOLLOW-UPS / TODOS (short list, keep these tight):
1) Update infra scheduler constraints to prefer GPU nodes with >12GB free margin when model-variant has memory profile > X (SRE-517) - owner: Hannah - due: 2026-11-10
2) Add pre-rollout check in CI to compare model artifact vram_req vs node capacity; fail fast if > threshold - owner: Diego - due: 2026-11-12
3) Edit the playbook section "model rollout memory checks" in Confluence CON-2345 to include nvidia-smi commands and a pointer to the autoscaler logs - owner: Hannah - due: 2026-11-09
4) Create a short run of scheduled stress test on eu pool during low traffic window to verify autoscaler behavior - owner: Diego - due: 2026-11-15
5) Add alert annotation for generation-5xx-rate that includes recent deploy ID and model-variant label (helps correlate faster) - owner: SRE team - due: 2026-11-11

NOTES TO SELF (quick tips for next rotation):
- When you see memory climb on GPUs, check recent deploy timestamps and the commit diff for any changes to batch size or memory hints.
- If draining less than 3 pods, prefer graceful drain + spin up with lighter memory footprint to avoid OOM thrash.
- Keep fallback policy duration conservative (start with 6h, reassess with data).

THINGS I WROTE INTO INC-8421 (short):
- Snapshot: 02:12-02:30 UTC, generation-5xx-rate peaked 6.2%, fading after pool drain.
- Suspected cause: new model-variant with increased per-worker memory usage scheduled onto constrained nodes.
- Mitigation: drained 2 pods and pinned fallback to model-variant-stable.
- Next steps: infra scheduler constraint, CI pre-rollout check, playbook update.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS:
- How did autoscaler choose to scale vs. rebalance? Need deeper query in autoscaler logs (where to look: infra/auto-logs in S3?).
- Were there any GPU driver updates on eu-gpu-03 around the same time? (quick check pending).

LINKS / ARTIFACTS I LEFT IN SLACK:
- Posted a short summary and metrics snapshot to #sre-paging thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01ABCDEF/p1700000000000
- Pinned the deploy commit in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/9a3b7

HANDOFF NOTES FOR DAY TEAM:
- See INC-8421 for full timeline + attached graphs.
- Prioritize SRE-517 edits and playbook doc change before next model rollout.
- If you need to rerun the drain, use cluster tag eu-gpu-pool-3a and watch GPU memory for 5 minutes after pod re-schedule.

RANDOM SCRATCHES (brain dump):
- Consider a CI gate: compare new model artifact memory hints vs cluster percentile (p90 GPU free).
- Quick metric query snippet to save in playbook: prometheus query used above.

END OF DOCKET.

-- H.P.
